applicability: any non-negative integer, in base 10; if the digit sum is still large, repeat the sum on it — the answer does not change

nulls.reason: The digit-sum test for divisibility by 3 is a theorem, not a heuristic. By the base-b digit-sum congruence (theorems.json id base-b-digit-sum-congruence) with b = 10, every non-negative integer n satisfies n ≡ digit_sum(n) (mod 9), and 3 | 9 gives n ≡ digit_sum(n) (mod 3). No non-negative integer breaks the rule, so there is no simple-form carry case to state. The rule may require iterating the digit sum on very large numbers, but that is a convenience of computation, not a case where the rule gives a wrong answer.
